items.headline: National Cancer Institute explainer for CSBA: Why and how to apply for SBIR
items.preview: The SBIR and STTR funding programs have been updated, offering new opportunities for biotech start-ups.
items.article:
The SBIR and STTR federal seed funding programs—essential to many biotech start-ups—have been updated with important changes that provide new opportunities to applicants.
These changes include a new Strategic Breakthrough Program, which can bring up to $30 million to impactful innovations addressing pediatric and rare cancers, experts from the National Cancer Institute (NCI) told a Sept. 17 webinar for the Council of State Bioscience Associations (CSBA).
Why this matters: The next application deadline is Jan. 5, making this information crucial for oncology biotechs and any biotech seeking seed funding to start their work.

items.headline: Mildly Alkaline Implant Surfaces Enlist Neutrophils to Fight Infection and Rebuild Bone
items.preview: A new titanium implant surface design recruits neutrophils to enhance antibacterial defense and promote bone healing.
items.article:
Orthopedic implants have transformed the treatment of fractures and bone defects, yet implant-associated infection remains a significant challenge. A new study proposes a titanium surface that recruits neutrophils to enhance host antibacterial defense without adding exogenous agents.
The researchers engineered a titanium surface that maintains a mildly alkaline pH, which promotes neutrophil activity and enhances their ability to form extracellular traps to capture pathogens. This approach not only reduces bacterial survival but also supports bone regeneration, offering a promising strategy for infected bone defects.
Why this matters: This innovative design could improve outcomes for patients facing infections associated with orthopedic implants.

items.headline: Roche, Ionis RNA drug scores in kidney disease study
items.preview: Roche and Ionis report positive Phase 3 trial results for their kidney disease drug, sefaxersen.
items.article:
Roche and Ionis Pharmaceuticals announced that their experimental drug for IgA nephropathy, sefaxersen, succeeded in a Phase 3 clinical trial, achieving significant improvements in protein levels in urine, a key indicator of kidney health.
The companies plan to present detailed data at an upcoming medical meeting and will continue monitoring participants for two years. If approved, sefaxersen will compete with other therapies in a growing market for IgA nephropathy treatments.
Why this matters: Sefaxersen's success could provide a new treatment option for patients with this challenging kidney disorder.

items.headline: Metabolite Fingerprint in Seminal Plasma Could Explain Hidden Male Infertility
items.preview: A systematic review identifies metabolites in seminal plasma that may reveal causes of male infertility.
items.article:
Male infertility accounts for about half of infertility cases, yet conventional semen analysis often fails to provide explanations. A new systematic review has cataloged metabolites in the seminal plasma of infertile men, revealing potential biomarkers for different infertility phenotypes.
The study identified 284 metabolites with distinct patterns associated with conditions like asthenozoospermia and oligozoospermia. This metabolic profiling could lead to better diagnostics and targeted treatments for male infertility.
Why this matters: Understanding the metabolic basis of infertility could transform clinical approaches and improve outcomes for couples facing unexplained infertility.

items.headline: Ancient inversion polymorphisms associate with sexually selected traits across natural guppy populations
items.preview: Study reveals how chromosomal inversions in guppies are linked to sexual selection and adaptation.
items.article:
This research investigates chromosomal inversions in guppies from Trinidad, finding 22 inversions associated with local adaptation to predation pressures. These inversions, which predate the colonization of the rivers, are linked to sexually selected traits, suggesting that sexual selection plays a role in maintaining genetic diversity.
The findings indicate that inversions can provide a reservoir of genetic variation that may be advantageous under changing environmental conditions.
Why this matters: Understanding the genetic basis of adaptation in guppies can shed light on evolutionary processes and the role of sexual selection in maintaining biodiversity.
